newsitem.title: UK: UK funds returning to Japan, Pacific, bulls of UK.
newsitem.headline: UK funds returning to Japan, Pacific, bulls of UK.

text.p: UK fund managers are back in Japan and the Pacific Basin, optimistic on the outlook for equities in both areas and looking to increase their holdings there, according to a poll conducted by Merrill Lynch.
The survey showed buyers of the region outnumbering sellers this month by 12 percent, where last month sellers outnumbered buyers by five percent.

UK funds are forecasting strong economic activity for 1997 with the average UK GDP growth estimated at 3.4 percent. The poll was conducted by Gallup between December 2-4 covering 75 institutions handling funds totalling 1.08 trillion stg.
Merrill said only five respondents expect the UK's economic situation to deteriorate over the next year.
On bonds, funds have turned net sellers of gilts after the November rally, with bears outnumbering bulls by 13 percent.
The funds said they were selling US equities but adding to European exposure, trimming their UK holdings. Many are still reducing cash balances and UK property is back in favour.
Among European equity markets, Germany was preferred on a 12-month outlook, with Switzerland least liked.

On the UK economy, most are expecting higher inflation and fully 100 percent of respondents see higher base rates in the next 12 months. The favoured currency for UK funds is the dollar, followed by sterling, yen and the mark.

Responding to a question on which party will win the general election, which must be held by May next year, the poll showed 89 percent expected Labour to win, against 11 percent backing the Conservative Party, unchanged from last month.
